title: PokeSurvivor Beginner Guide: Your First Stronger Run
description: Choose a first partner, understand active attacks, survive the early waves and decide when a chest or Rift is worth the risk.
imageAlt: Grass battlefield from the official PokeSurvivor game
outcomes: Enemy waves, bosses and world objects

sections.title: 1. Choose a partner you can learn with
paragraphs: To start Poke Survivor, open the Play page and launch the official game at pokesurvivor.com. Start as a guest or use the game’s own account options. This guide cannot read your save: available partners, purchased upgrades and collection progress are managed by the game.

Charmander begins with Ember, Squirtle with Water Gun and Bulbasaur with Vine Whip. They introduce a targeted projectile, a piercing stream and a close-range arc. Pick the opening style you can position safely. A large attack multiplier does not automatically make a partner easier to play.

Before starting, note your opening move and one evolution goal. Read its required stat card in Level-up Cards. Use the Pokédex for the partner’s actual starting HP, movement speed and attack factor; these differ from main-series Pokémon stats.

The moves listed here are defaults. In Upgrades, Starting move costs 400 coins once for that partner and then lets you change its opening attack for free. Choose a non-buff move from its legal pool, or keep the default even when it is an opening exception.

sections.title: 2. Move deliberately and switch the active slot
paragraphs: Move with WASD or the arrow keys on desktop. Select an attack slot with 1–4, cycle with Q/E or use the move icons. Esc pauses. On mobile, use landscape orientation, drag to move and tap the move icons. Give the battlefield enough screen space to see warning markers.

Only the selected slot triggers attacks. Learning four moves does not make all four cast together. Switch when the current attack no longer suits the approaching enemies. Some already-created projectiles or timed buffs can persist after switching; Bonds later let multiple moves cast from one active slot. Choice Band is an item exception that prevents ordinary slot switching while equipped.

Circle the edge of a group and keep a second exit in mind. Take nearby experience when the route is open. If a warning circle or line appears, leave it before returning for the pickup. Crossing the center of a horde for one experience gem often costs more health than the level is worth.

A controller can move, switch attacks, pause and operate menus; check Settings > Controls for your device. Automatic firing and automatic aiming are separate: Manual aim in Settings > Accessibility is off by default and lets a mouse or right stick control direction. Try it in open space before committing to a close-range attack.

figure.alt: PokeSurvivor battlefield with enemies and room to move around the player
figure.caption: Game battlefield: keep an escape route open before moving in for experience. This image illustrates positioning, not a fixed enemy spawn.

sections.title: 3. Give the opening minutes a clear job
paragraphs: Your first job is to establish a reliable attack and stay alive long enough to improve it. At a level-up, read all three offers: a new move changes your options, a move upgrade strengthens an existing attack, and a stat card helps the current run or satisfies an evolution condition.

Choose one main evolution instead of distributing early levels evenly across every available move. Ember, for example, needs level 5 and a Power card taken in the same run. The card can be taken before level 5. Once ready, select the gold evolution offer; permanent menu upgrades do not substitute for that run card.

If you are losing health because enemies survive too long, improving the main attack may help. If you are repeatedly trapped, change the route and attack spacing before assuming another damage card will fix it. Survival choices can justify delaying the planned evolution.

Check Physical or Special on the card as well as its type. A partner can learn a compatible attack that uses its weaker attack factor. For example, Machamp favors physical attacks such as Karate Chop; being able to learn Shadow Ball does not make its special damage equally strong. The Level-up page shows this difference for the partner you choose.

sections.title: 4. Read waves and bosses as changing pressure
paragraphs: Outside type-horde events, the game draws seven species per wild-enemy tier from overlapping base-stat-total bands. Later tiers join the pool while older casts continue with less weight. The schedule below describes eligibility, not a promise that a named species appears at that minute.

A healer or shielder can make an ordinary crowd harder to clear. A summoner adds bodies, a runner intercepts a predictable route and a bomber punishes staying close. Beam, jump and ground-zone warnings give you information: move out of the marked area first, then decide whether to attack or collect experience.

Boss slots in the game begin at 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15 minutes, with a different selection each run. The displayed HP and damage are templates before species, time, behavior, spawner and co-op modifiers. Use the candidate lists to recognize possibilities, not to predict exact fight length.

At 30:00, once any current Rift or card choice ends, the Judgment of Arceus begins. Arceus is invulnerable, and a new legendary joins every five seconds. Movement speed above 130 has only a quarter of its normal extra effect in this phase. Arceus accelerates further after five minutes; its contact damage rises after seven and can reach your full HP after ten. These are escalating hazards, not a fixed 40-minute end screen.

sections.title: 5. Stop for rewards only when you have an exit
paragraphs: A locked chest takes 3.5 seconds nearby to open in the game, and enemies keep attacking. Move away when the space closes; opening progress decays rather than forcing you to remain. Healing springs consume charge, while an altar grants a temporary effect instead of permanent strength.

A Rift takes you into a separate legendary arena. Each victory grants a Bond for move fusion; it does not automatically unlock a normal legendary partner. Check your health, attack and the arena’s 120-second limit before entering. Losing the challenge returns you to the map without the victory reward. New Rifts stop opening at 28:00 before the Judgment of Arceus.

Other events include type hordes, golden hour, rescues and fleeing treasure thieves. A timer or a shiny-looking reward does not make a chase safe. Check the event effects below before deciding whether to change your route.

sections.title: 6. Review the decision that ended the run
paragraphs: After a run, identify the immediate cause: a warning marker you stayed in, an escape lane you closed, an attack that did not cover the crowd, or insufficient damage against a durable enemy. Pick one change for the next attempt so you can tell whether it helped.

Run cards disappear after the run. Tickets expand the collection through regional banners; coins can buy upgrades for the selected partner. Spend according to your goal rather than treating every currency as interchangeable.

A useful first-run checklist is simple: know the active slot, keep a clear route, focus one evolution, select its required stat card and leave a dangerous reward behind when necessary. Review the upgrade cards and type chart before your next attempt.

sections.title: 7. Save before leaving or changing devices
paragraphs: With a signed-in account, changes are recorded in the current browser first. Cloud uploads are scheduled after about 30 minutes with pending changes. Finishing a run or making a gacha pull is no longer a promise of an immediate cloud upload.

Use Save at the top right before closing or switching devices. Check that the pending indicator clears. If a recent upload is still inside the minimum interval, the button may queue the next upload rather than finish immediately; wait for the status shown in the game. A guest session does not keep permanent progress.

title: PokeSurvivor Upgrade & Build Guide: Cards, Evolutions and Bonds
description: Build a compatible loadout, choose the right stat cards, unlock gold evolutions and use Bonds to free slots without wasting your upgrade choices.
imageAlt: Agility, Power and Poison Sting offered as level-up choices in PokeSurvivor
outcomes: Know what each card choice does

sections.title: 1. Start with the partner’s actual move pool
paragraphs: A normal level-up move pool combines Normal moves with the partner’s species types. A Fire partner can therefore see Normal and Fire options; a dual-type partner has both type families. Check the partner’s available moves in the game before choosing an evolution goal.

An opening exception can add a move outside that ordinary pool. Psyduck is Water but starts with Confusion. You can upgrade that opening move; it does not mean every Psychic move becomes available as a new card. Check the starting move and the normal pool separately.

Plan one main attack and one useful alternative before filling every slot. Attack behavior matters: a projectile, an orbit and a dash solve different positioning problems. A type advantage is useful only when you can actually place the attack where it needs to land.

Starting move is a 400-coin upgrade bought separately for each partner. After unlocking it, you can choose a non-buff opening from that partner’s pool, including its original default. New-move cards no longer switch your active attack automatically; change slots yourself when you want the new move.

sections.title: 2. Match Physical and Special to your partner
paragraphs: Move type and attack category answer different questions. Fire, Water and the other types determine matchups and weather; Physical or Special determines which attack factor your partner uses and which defense the target uses. Your partner’s old single attack factor is the higher of its physical and special factors.

Swords Dance and Dragon Dance boost physical attack only. Nasty Plot boosts special attack and belongs to the Normal pool, so every partner can receive it. It does not help the damage of a physical attack. Choose a buff for the damaging moves you actually intend to use together.

The percentage beside a move in Level-up compares your partner’s attack factor for that category with its stronger factor. It is not a hit chance or measured DPS. Range, number of hits, enemy defenses, type and weather still affect the result.

Single-type partners now deal 20% more damage with moves matching their own type. Other types in their pool do not get this bonus, and dual-type partners do not receive it. This is separate from attack-category fit, enemy typing and weather.

table.caption: Separate the category, the type and the buff before choosing a card.
rows: Machamp has a stronger physical factor; these two attacks do not use the same factor.
Useful only for the physical damage in your active slot or Bond group.
Raises special damage; it does not strengthen physical hits.

sections.title: 3. Learn what the three offers can change
paragraphs: A new-move card fills an empty slot with a compatible move. An upgrade card raises an owned move by one level, to a maximum of 5. A stat card improves the run or heals immediately. Each move has its own upgrade effects; a later level can increase count, coverage or uptime rather than simply add damage.

Only the active slot triggers moves. A new move gives you another attack to switch to, rather than automatically casting alongside the old one. Existing projectiles and timed buffs may continue briefly after switching. The game stops offering additional buff moves once you hold two; learn a damaging attack before relying on a support move.

Stat cards have different limits. Power can be picked 40 times, Sprint 8 and Reflexes 10 in this game build. Armor has a 12-pick limit and a separate 70% application cap. Percentage effects such as Power compound, so a pick count is not the same as an additive percentage.

The game first samples up to six eligible new moves. Attacks on your partner’s stronger side receive sampling weight 2 instead of 1; buff moves also receive weight 2. The later three-card draw uses its own weights. This favors suitable attacks without guaranteeing one or doubling its final appearance probability.

figure.alt: Agility, Power and Poison Sting offered as upgrade choices in PokeSurvivor
figure.caption: An earlier game card screen showing three choices. The current version also labels damaging moves as Physical or Special.

sections.title: 4. Reach both evolution requirements in the same run
paragraphs: An eligible move must reach level 5, and you must have selected at least one copy of its required stat card during the current run. You may take the stat card before or after level 5. Then choose its gold evolution card at a later level-up.

There are 103 base moves and 97 evolution paths; the six buff moves do not evolve. A ready evolution is given a guaranteed place among the offered cards for the first ready candidate. If several moves are ready, do not interpret that as every evolution appearing together.

One stat card can satisfy several recipes that use it, but each move still needs its own levels and gold choice. Ember and Water Gun both use Power. Confusion uses Reflexes. Use the examples below and the full Level-up list rather than guessing the requirement from the move’s type.

sections.title: 5. Pick upgrades for a problem, not a perfect sequence
paragraphs: Concentrate early move upgrades on one main attack and take its prerequisite when it appears. Once the first evolution is established, decide whether to improve coverage, movement or sustain. Card offers are random, so the plan must tolerate an alternative.

If a good defensive or recovery choice keeps the run alive, it can be more useful than waiting for a specific attack. Avoid collecting several incompatible goals simply because the cards look strong in isolation. A second evolution is valuable only if you can finish it and make use of its slot.

Use the expanded Level-up rows to compare what each next level changes. Raw per-hit damage is not a DPS ranking: cooldown, projectile count, area, pierce, enemy typing and your partner’s attack factor all affect the result. Use the Types page to compare an attack against each of an enemy’s defending types, multiplying the two factors for a dual-type target.

sections.title: 6. Use a Bond to free a slot
paragraphs: Each Rift victory grants a Bond. After returning from the arena, you can fuse two separate learned moves, then spend later Bonds to add a loose move to an unfinished group. A group holds up to four moves and the selected group casts together. One Bond does not immediately fuse four moves.

Fusion frees the slot previously occupied by a separate move, allowing new-move cards to appear again. It does not supply an unlearned move, free levels or an evolution. If fewer than two suitable separate moves exist, the Bond waits until you have a valid fusion choice.

Fuse attacks you want active at the same time, while keeping a deliberate alternative slot for a different situation. Enter a Rift when the current run is ready for its risk; having an appealing fusion planned is not itself a reason to enter with low health.

sections.title: 7. Use rerolls and save a flexible plan
paragraphs: You get one free card reroll per run. Purchased Card reroll levels add up to five more, for a maximum of six. Defeating a boss does not add another reroll in this game version. Ban can exclude up to three new moves for a partner. Repertoire adds a random eligible non-buff attack at the start, occupying a second slot.

These menu purchases are separate from run stat cards: owning a permanent Strength upgrade does not count as taking Power during the current run. When a gold card seems missing, check the owned move’s level and the exact prerequisite first.

Choose a partner and check its move pool before planning four compatible slots. Compare the Level-up evolution requirements, then note which stat cards the attacks share. Keep one alternative for a missing card instead of depending on a perfect sequence.

title: PokeSurvivor Collection Guide: Tickets, Gacha and Missions
description: Earn tickets through missions and achievements, understand 70-pull pity and ten-pull rules, choose a regional target and claim useful mission rewards.
outcomes: Use daily and weekly mission rewards

sections.title: 1. Separate tickets, coins and collection goals
paragraphs: Tickets are used for regional gacha pulls. Coins are a different resource used for partner progression. A single ticket and a ×10 ticket also have different batch behavior: ten separate single pulls do not receive the special last-result guarantee of a ten-pull batch.

Choose a collection goal before spending. If you want one species, find its region and rarity in the Pokédex, then select the corresponding regional banner. If you mainly want any rare partner, that is a different probability question from targeting one specific species.

Use the game to inspect current balances and claim rewards. This site cannot read your save, move tickets between accounts or make pulls on your behalf. Review the banner rules and guarantees in this guide before choosing a ticket budget.

sections.title: 2. Read the base rates and the regional pool
paragraphs: The base rarity rates are 45% for 1★, 30% for 2★, 17% for 3★, 6.5% for 4★ and 1.5% for 5★. Inside a rarity tier, eligible species in that regional pool have equal selection weight. Different regions contain different numbers of species at each rarity.

A target’s ordinary per-pull chance is the rarity rate divided by the number of eligible partners at that rarity in the banner. That is a baseline before pity or a batch guarantee changes the rarity roll. Do not multiply an ordinary chance by a large number of pulls and call it a guaranteed result.

For example, Pikachu is a 2-star Kanto partner. Kanto has 41 partners at that rarity, so its ordinary single-pull chance is 30% ÷ 41, about 0.7317%. Pity or the restricted last result of a ten-pull changes the rarity roll; this baseline is not the chance for every position in a batch.

links.label: Find a species and its banner

sections.title: 3. Understand what pity and ten-pulls promise
paragraphs: The counter is checked after it increments: at 69 without a 5★ result, the next pull is forced to 5★. A 5★ result resets the counter. Pity is tracked by regional banner, so use the value shown for the banner you intend to pull.

A ten-pull has a separate floor. If its first nine results contain no 4★ or 5★, the tenth result is restricted to those two rarities, using their relative 6.5:1.5 weights. That means 81.25% for 4★ and 18.75% for 5★ on that restricted roll, unless pity already forces 5★.

A guaranteed rarity does not guarantee a particular species. Seventy pulls can guarantee at least one 5★ under these rules without guaranteeing your chosen legendary. When comparing budgets, keep the goal set to the actual species rather than reading the any-5★ result as target odds.

sections.title: 4. Build a reward routine you can complete
paragraphs: Runs, achievements, completed missions and world rewards all contribute to progression. Choose a few attainable objectives for the partner and route you are already practicing. Repeated short, successful objectives can be more useful than attempting a long run you cannot yet finish reliably.

The game’s locked chest requires 3.5 seconds nearby and drops 1–3 single tickets, with separate rolls for an extra ×10 ticket and a held item. A thief may carry coins or a ×10 ticket. These rewards require surviving and collecting them; do not treat a risky chase as free income.

Achievement rewards are granted automatically when their conditions are detected; completed mission rewards need a manual claim in the Missions screen. Read the objective before starting: a type-specific defeat target, a single-run survival target and a cumulative count require different behavior. Compare the mission goals below before choosing a route.

sections.title: 5. Plan around daily and weekly templates
paragraphs: You receive three daily missions and two weekly missions, drawn from ten daily and six weekly possibilities. Each assignment receives one of the listed target values; some also receive a Pokémon type. Calendar periods use Europe/Madrid and selection varies by account. The goals below show the possible assignments; check your current ones in the game.

Survival, level and play-with-a-type objectives keep the best qualifying single-run result. Defeats, chests, coins, evolutions and similar objectives accumulate qualifying progress. Run-end values such as time and coins are processed when a run ends.

Completing a target and claiming its reward are separate steps. Open the Missions screen to claim. The game allows one daily replacement per day, excluding objectives already in the current daily set. A weekly completed-dailies objective advances through claimed daily missions.

sections.title: 6. Treat shiny appearance as a separate goal
paragraphs: Eligible gacha selections use a 1% shiny check. Ordinary wild spawns and scheduled map bosses use 1 in 4,096, while a Rift legendary has its own 1-in-512 check when selected. Shiny artwork must exist. Enemy shinies must be defeated before the form is collected; merely seeing one does not unlock it.

If a rolled shiny is already owned, the game tries a missing shiny in the same region and rarity. When that pool is exhausted, it can return a normal result. Do not plan income around an unconditional triple-refund promise for every completed shiny pool.

The available game artwork contains shiny sprites for 958 of the 966 roster species. Missing artwork is explicitly marked in the Pokédex. A color variation does not change the partner’s base stats. Compare the actual sprites below and pursue a shiny after deciding whether collection breadth or that cosmetic target matters more.

links.label: Read the full shiny hunting guide

sections.title: 7. Before the next pull
paragraphs: Confirm the banner, name the target and read that banner’s current pity counter. Choose single or ten-pull mode correctly. Use a budget you already have, then compare the target result with the any-5★ result so the two goals stay separate.

After pulling, check new partners, duplicate coin refunds and the current regional pity counter in the game before planning another batch. A 5★ result resets that region’s pity counter. If your collection goal changes, check the new target’s region and rarity pool before choosing a banner. Before changing devices, press Save and check the upload status. A pull is recorded locally first; the next automatic cloud upload can still be pending.

For the next run, return to the same simple progression loop: choose a partner you can use well, finish compatible objectives, claim completed rewards and spend toward a specific goal. A larger collection adds options; practiced movement and card choices make those options useful.

title: How to Get Shiny Pokémon in PokeSurvivor
heading: How to Get Shiny Pokémon
description: Find shinies in wild encounters, legendary Rifts and regional gacha. Compare the three rates, collect the form you find and keep your account progress safe.
imageAlt: Illustrated field guide showing the real normal and shiny Charizard and Eevee sprites

seo.title: PokeSurvivor Shiny Guide - Wild, Rift and Gacha Odds
seo.description: Learn how to get shiny Pokémon in PokeSurvivor through wild encounters, Rifts and gacha. Compare odds, duplicate rules, saving and equipping your partner.

outcomes: Three shiny routes, each with its own roll
A safe wild-hunting plan and practical ticket choices
Duplicate rules, co-op rewards, saving and equipping

sections.title: 1. Choose between wild encounters, Rifts and gacha
paragraphs: You can unlock a shiny by defeating a shiny enemy during a run, defeating a shiny legendary in a Rift or receiving a shiny result from a regional gacha banner. You do not need to own the normal form first: getting a new shiny also unlocks that species in its normal form.

If you want your first shiny of any species, combine ordinary runs with tickets earned along the way. If you want one favorite, first check its region and rarity. Neither route lets you name the next shiny that will appear, and a higher rarity does not make a result more likely to be shiny.

table.caption: Three acquisition routes, three separate rolls. Seeing an enemy is not the defeat needed to collect it.
rows: Defeat the shiny enemy while staying alive.
Defeat the shiny legendary within the arena time limit.
1 in 100 after an eligible species is selected
Spend tickets in the correct region; inspect the result.

callout.title: Sign in before a serious hunt
callout.text: Use the official game’s account options before collecting. Guest progress is not saved. A shiny found in a guest session is not a reliable way to build a lasting collection.

sections.title: 2. How to catch a wild shiny
paragraphs: The shiny check happens when an eligible enemy spawns. Killing an ordinary enemy does not turn it shiny afterward. A shiny uses its alternate palette and sparkle effects; a shiny appearing through the regular enemy spawner also triggers an announcement and sound. Scheduled bosses can pass the shiny check too, so keep watching during boss fights.

The unlock happens when the shiny is defeated. Walking into it, seeing the announcement or collecting an unrelated item does not count. There is no separate Poké Ball interaction to perform in this capture flow.
steps: Start with a partner and main attack you can control comfortably. A hunt ends quickly if you cannot keep an escape lane open.
When the alert appears, locate the sparkling enemy without crossing the center of the horde. Clear nearby threats if they block the route.
Choose the active move that fits the distance and matchup. Keep attacking from a safe angle rather than standing on the target.
Allow more time to finish it: the shiny enemy modifier doubles its HP and multiplies its XP by five relative to that enemy before the shiny modifier. Existing difficulty and boss scaling still apply.
After defeating it, check the acquisition message, the run’s caught-shiny display and your collection. Before leaving or changing devices, press Save and confirm the upload status.

callout.title: Golden enemies are a different effect
callout.text: Golden Hour changes enemy rewards; it is not a shiny-rate boost. A gold-colored effect, a ticket sound or a sparkling UI reward alone does not confirm that a shiny species joined your collection.

sections.title: 3. Hunt a legendary shiny inside a Rift
paragraphs: Rift legendaries use their own shiny check: 1 in 512 when the arena selects a legendary with shiny artwork. This is eight times the ordinary wild rate per eligible check. It does not mean eight times as many shinies per hour: Rifts appear far less often than regular enemies, and you still have to win the fight.

The opponent and its shiny form are selected when the arena starts. The roll does not repeat every second, whenever you attack or each time you switch moves. A normal legendary cannot turn shiny because you keep the fight going.

Defeat the shiny legendary to unlock its shiny and normal partner forms. Defeating an ordinary legendary records the victory for relevant goals, but does not directly give you that normal partner. An arena victory and ownership are different collection records.

Rift selection favors legendaries you have not defeated: their selection weight is 4, compared with 1 for a previously defeated opponent. That preference uses victory records, not your missing-shiny list. It neither guarantees the next species nor raises the selected legendary’s 1-in-512 shiny roll.
steps: Enter with enough health and damage for the arena, rather than treating its better per-check rate as a reason to risk every run.
Read the arena’s terrain, weather and attack markers. You have 120 seconds to defeat its legendary; a shiny version has the usual shiny enemy HP modifier.
Defeat the shiny before the arena fails and confirm its entry in your collection. Use Save and check its status before leaving or moving to another device.

callout.title: Rift access has its own limits
callout.text: The checked build stops opening new Rifts at 28:00 ahead of the Judgment of Arceus. An existing portal is temporary, and a living map boss delays new opening checks. A failed arena returns you to the map; it is not a successful shiny capture. The Judgment’s legendary waves use a different encounter flow and do not receive this Rift shiny roll.

sections.title: 4. Use tickets without confusing rarity and shininess
paragraphs: Open the game’s gacha and choose the region containing your target. A single pull costs one regular ticket. A ten-pull uses ten regular tickets or one ×10 ticket. Coins are not the currency used for those pulls.

The game chooses a rarity, then a species from that regional rarity pool, then checks whether that species has a shiny form. When it does, the normal shiny check is 1%. A species without a shiny form cannot become shiny through that check.

Ten-pulls guarantee at least one 4-star-or-higher result, not a shiny. Each regional banner also has a 5-star pity counter: from a counter of zero, the 70th pull is forced to 5-star if no earlier 5-star reset it. That rarity guarantee does not replace the shiny roll.

Do not read a featured portrait as a targeted shiny banner. For example, Pikachu is a 2-star Kanto partner, and the current Kanto pool has 41 species at that rarity. Before duplicate redirection, an ordinary non-guaranteed pull has a base shiny-Pikachu chance of 30% ÷ 41 × 1%, about 0.00732% (roughly 1 in 13,667). A ten-pull’s last-slot rule, pity and your existing shiny collection can change which result you ultimately receive.
bullets: Stay on the target’s region if that is the partner you care about. Pulling a different region cannot directly select it.
Use ten-pulls when you also value the rarity floor. They do not increase the 1% shiny check itself.
A long dry streak does not create a hidden shiny guarantee. The displayed pity counter tracks 5-star rarity, not shinies.

sections.title: 5. What the odds mean over many attempts
paragraphs: A 1-in-100 check is not a promise of one shiny every 100 pulls. Independent attempts can produce an early shiny, several close together or a long stretch without one. The same reasoning applies to wild encounters: 4,096 eligible spawns do not guarantee a shiny.

The table models at least one successful shiny roll using 1 − (1 − p)^n. For wild rows, count eligible spawns, not kills or minutes. For Rift rows, count eligible legendary selections, not every enemy defeated in the arena. Gacha rows assume every selected species has shiny artwork. These are theoretical roll probabilities, not measured run results or the probability of a particular new shiny.

table.caption: Illustrative cumulative probabilities, rounded to two decimals; no guarantee is created at any row.

callout.title: A successful roll can still return a normal gacha result
callout.text: If the selected shiny is already owned and every shiny in that regional rarity pool is collected, the game falls back to a normal result. The table therefore does not promise a new collection entry, even after a successful shiny check.

sections.title: 6. What happens if you already own the shiny?
paragraphs: Enemy captures and gacha results handle duplicates differently. Ordinary wild and Rift shinies share the enemy-defeat capture flow. This matters when deciding whether to chase a shiny you recognize or keep spending tickets in a nearly complete regional pool.

For gacha, the replacement search stays within the selected banner and rarity. It does not choose a missing shiny from another region or give you a free choice. If the first selected species has no shiny art, the game does not run this duplicate-redirection step to rescue the roll.

table.caption: Follow the actual reward branch rather than assuming every duplicate has a triple-coin payout.
rows: Unlocks its shiny form and its normal form if missing.
Adds 300 coins to the current run; no second collection copy.
Gacha rolls an already-owned shiny; alternatives remain
Selects a missing shiny from the same regional rarity pool.
Gacha rolls an already-owned shiny; that pool is complete
Falls back to normal. A new normal species unlocks; an owned normal uses its normal rarity refund.

callout.title: About the “triple coins” wording
callout.text: Some public descriptions mention triple coins for a duplicate shiny. The checked draw logic redirects owned shinies or falls back to normal before that payout branch. Do not plan a ticket-spending strategy around receiving triple refunds.

sections.title: 7. Compare the actual normal and shiny forms
paragraphs: The comparison below uses the game’s Idle animation frames and its original collection star effect. The game draws those stars separately from the shiny sprite sheet. Some palette changes are obvious; others are subtle. Check the Shiny label and collection status alongside the color.
These examples help you decide which partner to pursue. They are not a list of boosted-rate targets. Your preferred appearance does not change a banner’s probability.

sections.title: 8. Build a repeatable hunting routine
paragraphs: Start by choosing the goal: any first shiny, a specific partner or more missing forms in one region. Those are different projects. An encounter that helps a broad collection might do nothing for the one species you want.

For wild hunting, prioritize runs you can keep under control. Clear enemies efficiently and keep moving so you can respond when an alert appears. Do not reset a healthy run simply because no shiny appeared in the opening minutes; the next eligible check does not become better because the previous ones failed.

For gacha, earn tickets while working on useful missions and achievements. Check completed mission rewards and claim them in the game. Regular enemy drops, bosses and Rifts can also contribute tickets, but no fixed number of minutes guarantees a particular ticket or shiny reward.

If you target a species through encounters, remember that ordinary enemy casts and Rift opponents use different pools. A high kill count against other species is not the same as many chances at your favorite. For legendary shinies, count the Rifts that actually select a shiny-capable legendary; their 1-in-512 roll does not apply to all enemies in a run.
steps: Sign in, check your target’s region and compare the appearance you want.
Choose a reliable survival build and one mission objective that fits it.
React to wild shiny alerts safely, and take prepared Rift fights for legendary targets. Defeat the shiny before treating it as collected.
Claim earned tickets, choose the intended regional banner and inspect your results.
Confirm new entries, equip the desired form, press Save and wait until the game no longer shows pending progress.

sections.title: 9. Equip your shiny and protect the unlock
paragraphs: After an unlock, select that Pokémon in the official game’s collection. Its Normal/Shiny selector appears when you own the shiny form. Switch to Shiny and choose it as your partner. The main partner panel also has a Normal/Shiny control for an owned shiny, which is useful on mobile.

A shiny partner uses the same species stats and move pool. The extra HP and XP described earlier belong to shiny enemies; choosing a shiny appearance does not give your player double health or five times the experience.

A capture is recorded when the shiny is defeated; it does not wait for the run to end. With an account, that local record and a completed cloud upload are separate. Automatic uploads are scheduled after about 30 minutes with pending changes. Press Save at the top right, then wait for the pending status to clear before switching devices or closing. A recent upload can briefly delay another one. Guests do not keep permanent progress.

In the checked co-op flow, the host broadcasts the shiny-capture event to connected clients. It is a shared event rather than a final-hit contest. Stay connected and confirm the unlock in your own collection afterward; a teammate’s screenshot is not confirmation that your account saved it.

callout.title: The fan-site preview does not change your save
callout.text: Switching the sprite appearance on this site’s Pokédex only previews the artwork. It does not unlock a shiny, spend tickets or equip a partner in the official game.

sections.title: 10. Shiny hunting questions

questions.question: Can a Rift legendary be shiny?
questions.answer: Yes. Each eligible legendary selection has a separate 1-in-512 check. Defeat the shiny legendary to unlock it. Neither 512 attempts nor a normal legendary victory guarantees its shiny form.

questions.question: Do I need a Poké Ball or a special capture item?
questions.answer: No separate capture item is used in the checked wild or Rift shiny flow. Defeat the shiny enemy; the unlock is granted by that defeat event.

questions.question: Is a shiny guaranteed after 100 pulls?
questions.answer: No. At a constant 1% rate, 100 eligible independent checks give about a 63.40% chance of at least one successful shiny roll, before collection-related fallbacks. That is not a species guarantee.

questions.question: Does the 70-pull pity make the result shiny?
questions.answer: No. That counter guarantees a 5-star rarity result. A separate shiny check still applies, and a 5-star resets that regional rarity counter.

questions.question: Can I get a shiny before owning the normal Pokémon?
questions.answer: Yes. A newly granted shiny also unlocks the normal species if you did not own it.

questions.question: Does Golden Hour, a stronger build or a long streak improve the rate?
questions.answer: The checked shiny rolls do not use those factors as rate bonuses. A stronger build can help you survive and finish an encounter; it does not turn the 1-in-4,096 spawn roll into better odds.

questions.question: Why is there no Shiny button for my partner?
questions.answer: Check that you actually own that partner’s shiny form in the official game, rather than just its normal form or a preview on this site. A species also needs supported shiny art. Confirm you are signed into the same account that earned it.

questions.question: Will I lose a captured shiny if I die afterward?
questions.answer: The unlock is triggered at the defeat, not awarded only for finishing a run. Keep the account signed in, press Save and confirm the upload status before leaving. A guest session or interrupted save is a separate persistence risk.
